title: terraform-vpc-sentry-module-subnets-nat-failover-endpoint-probes
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a reusable Terraform module (module name: redwood/vpc-sentry) that codifies VPC networking patterns for Private deployments. The module will provision: multi-AZ public/private subnets, configurable NAT/IGW topology, VPC endpoints (interface and gateway where appropriate), granular route tables, and an opinionated health-checking layer.

Goals:
- Provide a single module that supports both compact and wide topologies (1-3 AZs) with deterministic route priorities.
- Support cost-sensitive and cost-optimized options (managed NAT Gateway vs. autoscaling NAT instances) with clear trade-offs surfaced to users.
- Embed active egress health probes and endpoint reachability checks so higher-level automation can detect and remediate routing failures before customer traffic hits application tiers.
- Make upgrades safe: add lifecycle hooks and a non-destructive upgrade path for route table/endpoint changes that avoids mass replacement of subnets or IGWs.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- NAT: Default to AWS-managed NAT Gateway for simplicity and reliability. Provide an opt-in "nat_instance" strategy that wires an ASG + bootstrap script for customers that have strong cost constraints and are comfortable managing instances. Trade-off: NAT instances save cost but increase operational burden (security patches, scaling).
- Egress failover: Module will support a primary IGW + secondary NAT Gateway pattern per AZ and optional cross-AZ route mirroring for rapid failover. Implemented via route table entries with weighted route priorities and CloudWatch alarm-triggered Lambda re-route actions (lifted via outputs so infra teams can wire their remediation).
- Endpoints: Create interface endpoints for SQS/SecretsManager/KMS (configurable list) and gateway endpoints for S3/DynamoDB. Add support for cross-account endpoints by exposing an "allowed_principals" variable.
- Health checks: Use a combination of lightweight synthetic probes (Terraform-managed synthetic-checks resource entries that register a CloudWatch Synthetics canary or Route53 health checks depending on account feature flags) and route/attachment health validations. Probes are optional and default to off for small stacks.
- Upgrade path: Implement data-driven change detection (compare planned route/endpoint diffs) and emit a "module.change_plan" output summarizing risky replacements. Provide a documented canary rollout (apply to a single AZ with traffic-shift instructions) in the README.

Terraform contract (variables & outputs):
- Variables: vpc_id, az_list, public_cidr_map, private_cidr_map, create_nat (bool), nat_strategy ("gateway"|"instance"), endpoint_services (list), enable_health_checks (bool), probe_config (json string for advanced users), tags (map)
- Outputs: subnet_ids (public/private), route_table_ids, endpoint_ids, nat_gateway_ids, healthcheck_resources, change_plan_summary

Testing & validation:
- Unit: terratest suite validating route propagation, endpoint attachment, and tagging across AZ counts (1,2,3).
- Integration: deploy in a sandbox account, simulate AZ NAT failure (detach/update route) and verify canary probes detect failure and Lambda re-route executes successfully.
- Load smoke: verify that NAT instance strategy can saturate target throughput for smaller instance families; document limits.

Operational runbook (draft):
1) Deploy module version X to staging with enable_health_checks=true and probe targets="https://s3-redwood-probe.example".
2) Observe CloudWatch alarms and synthetic canary results in Console.
3) Perform upgrade to X+1 in a single AZ, confirm change_plan_summary shows no destructive changes.
4) Promote across AZs after 24h with traffic-shift.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module passes terratest assertions for route/endpoint idempotency in 3 AZ topologies.
- Canary healthchecks detect simulated egress failures and produce actionable alarms within 2 minutes.
- Module provides a clear non-destructive upgrade summary output and a documented canary rollout in README.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/VPC+Sentry+Module (internal)
- Design diagram (draw.io): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/vpc-sentry-design
- Proposed GH repo/initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-module-vpc-sentry/pull/12

Next steps:
- Spike: implement minimal prototype that creates subnets + one gateway endpoint + a mocked health check (2d).
- Review: sync with Security (required) to validate KMS/endpoint policies and cross-account constraints (1d).
- Implementation: full module and terratest harness (6d).
- Docs & runbook: 2d.
